transcript.content: Hi, it’s nice to meet you. What brings you in today?

Nice to meet you too. Well, my family brought me in because of what happened at the fair. 

I was giving my talk, and... well, I climbed up onto the tractor. I kept jerking the controls around because I was trying to show the crowd the new pattern. But the problem was, I couldn't make myself stop. Even with folks yelling at me to get down and quit it, I just kept doing it. So, they decided I needed to come see you.
Right before you start making those jerking movements, do you feel a strong urge or buildup inside that you have to let out?

No, I don't get any kind of urge or feeling like that. It's not like a pressure building up inside me or anything. I was just up there, and my hands were moving the levers. I didn't feel anything special right before it happened... I just couldn't get myself to quit doing it once I started.
Do you ever make repeated sounds or words that come out on their own?

No, I don't. I haven't ever noticed doing anything like that. I don't make noises or say words without meaning to. It was really just my hands and arms acting up with the tractor controls. I don't have any trouble with sounds coming out on their own.
When someone distracts you or your attention shifts to something else, do the jerking movements stop?

I'm not really sure about that. I mean... folks were yelling at me pretty loud at the fair, trying to get my attention so I'd come down. That didn't stop me at all. I just kept right on moving the levers. So I guess... no, people trying to distract me didn't seem to make it quit.
When this happens, does it feel like you are choosing to do the movements, or like your body is doing them on its own?

Well, I'm not rightly sure how to explain it. It didn't feel like I was sitting there deciding to do it... but I don't know if I'd say my body was just acting all on its own, either. I just know my hands were moving those levers and I couldn't make myself stop. I wasn't really thinking about choosing to do it, it was just happening.
When this happens, do you stay fully aware of what’s going on around you?

Well... I suppose I was aware of some things, since I could hear the folks yelling at me like I mentioned. But to say I was fully aware? I just don't know. My mind was pretty locked in on those levers and what my hands were doing. I can't rightly say I was taking in much else of what was going on around me.
Do you have any gaps in your memory for what happened while you were on the tractor?

No, I don't think I have any missing time or anything like that. I remember climbing up there, and I remember my hands on the levers... and like I said, I remember hearing people hollering at me from the ground. So, no, I don't have any gaps. I remember what happened just fine, it's just... I couldn't stop what my hands were doing.
Did this happen during a time when you were under a lot of stress or upset about something?

Well... no, I wouldn't say so. I wasn't upset about anything that I can think of. It was just a normal day out doing my regular work on the farm. I don't recall being under any extra stress or anything like that before it all started.
When you were moving those tractor levers, did it feel pleasurable or satisfying?

No... no, I wouldn't say that. There wasn't anything pleasurable about it. It wasn't satisfying or anything like that. I wasn't getting a kick out of it... it was just happening, and like I said, I just couldn't stop my hands from doing it.
